record.original_question: If f in S and f ′ is also univalent in D, what can be said about max |an |, n ≥ 2? The function z(1 − z)−1 shows that max |an | ≥ 1 whenever n ≥ 2. (J. G. Clunie) ′ ′

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and let $S$ be the class of functions
$$f(z)=z+\sum_{n=2}^{\infty}a_n z^n$$
that are analytic and univalent (one-to-one) on $\mathbb{D}$. Consider the subclass
$$S' = \{\, f\in S : f' \text{ is also univalent on } \mathbb{D}\,\}.$$
For each integer $n\geq 2$, determine
$$M_n := \sup_{f\in S'} |a_n|.$$
The function $f(z)=z(1-z)^{-1}=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} z^n$ belongs to $S'$ and shows $M_n\geq 1$ for every $n\geq 2$. Find sharp upper bounds for $|a_n|$ when $f\in S'$, and identify the extremal functions.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a definitive resolution of this classical question (attributed to J. G. Clunie) on coefficient bounds in the class of univalent functions whose derivative is also univalent. Related work on coefficient estimates in subclasses of $S$ exists, but no source confirming a sharp value of $\sup|a_n|$ for the class $\{f\in S: f' \text{ univalent}\}$ for all $n\geq 2$ was located, so the status appears unresolved.

status_evidence.snippet: The coefficient problem for a class of functions regular in the unit disk consists in determining... sharp bounds for these coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: General coefficient problems in subclasses of S remain a focus of research; no resolution for the f' univalent subclass was found.

status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among research problems without a noted solution.
